io_server_version: Writes the compile-time `IOKIT_SERVER_VERSION` constant and returns success. The visible body does not validate `main_port` or negotiate features; admission by the surrounding MIG/kobject transport is distinct from this wrapper's implementation. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2431).
io_object_get_class: Rejects a null object, asks the retained runtime object for its metaclass, and returns `kIOReturnNotFound` if that lookup is absent. Otherwise `strlcpy` copies the class name into the fixed `io_name_t` result. This reports the dynamic metaclass of the supplied object rather than searching the class registry by string. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2441).
io_object_get_superclass: Requires the main-device port and nonnull input/output arrays, interns the requested class name, and uses `copyMetaClassWithName` to hold the metaclass during lookup. It copies the superclass name only if both superclass and name exist. The temporary symbol and metaclass hold are released on all exits; unresolved classes or root classes return `kIOReturnNotFound`. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2463).
io_object_get_bundle_identifier: Requires the main-device port, interns the class name and acquires its metaclass. It obtains `getKmodName`, copies that symbol's string into the bounded output and returns success only when all lookups succeed. The temporary symbol and metaclass reference are released afterward. This answers the runtime class's kmod association, not a filesystem bundle search. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2514).
io_object_conforms_to: Rejects a null input object and evaluates `object->metaCast(className)`. The Boolean result reports whether the runtime object conforms to the named class; a false result is still a successful RPC. The wrapper neither allocates a new instance nor returns a second object capability. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2565).
io_object_get_retain_count: Rejects a null input and reads `getRetainCount` into the scalar result. This is a diagnostic snapshot of the runtime object's reference count while the call holds its input object; it is not a Mach send-right user-reference count and does not itself change ownership. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2581).
io_iterator_next: Distinguishes an `IOUserIterator`, whose `copyNextObject` already returns a retained object, from a plain `OSIterator`, whose borrowed `getNextObject` result is explicitly retained. Other objects yield `kIOReturnBadArgument`. A present result is handed to the output translation with success; exhaustion returns `kIOReturnNoDevice` rather than an unretained object. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2595).
io_iterator_reset: The `CHECK` macro requires an `OSIterator`; otherwise the RPC fails with a bad argument. The wrapper calls the iterator's virtual `reset` and returns success. Iterator-specific traversal invalidation, locking and retained collection behavior belong to that implementation rather than being independently reconstructed by this wrapper. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2627).
io_iterator_is_valid: Requires an `OSIterator`, reads its virtual `isValid` result and returns that Boolean with RPC success. Invalid traversal state is therefore represented in the output value, not as a generic transport failure; callers can decide whether to reset or discard the iterator. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2639).
io_service_get_matching_services: This exact legacy string-form body immediately returns `kIOReturnUnsupported`. The existence of similarly named binary or out-of-line forms does not make this declaration operational; no dictionary is parsed and no matching or notification registration is performed here. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2766).
io_service_get_matching_service: This exact legacy string-form body immediately returns `kIOReturnUnsupported`. The existence of similarly named binary or out-of-line forms does not make this declaration operational; no dictionary is parsed and no matching or notification registration is performed here. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2849).
io_service_match_property_table: This exact legacy string-form body immediately returns `kIOReturnUnsupported`. The existence of similarly named binary or out-of-line forms does not make this declaration operational; no dictionary is parsed and no matching or notification registration is performed here. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2685).
io_service_add_notification: This exact legacy string-form body immediately returns `kIOReturnUnsupported`. The existence of similarly named binary or out-of-line forms does not make this declaration operational; no dictionary is parsed and no matching or notification registration is performed here. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2995).
io_service_add_notification_64: This exact legacy string-form body immediately returns `kIOReturnUnsupported`. The existence of similarly named binary or out-of-line forms does not make this declaration operational; no dictionary is parsed and no matching or notification registration is performed here. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3009).
io_service_get_matching_services_bin: The common helper requires `main_device_port`, unserializes the supplied bounded buffer, and requires an `OSDictionary`. It applies task compatibility matching, calls `IOService::getMatchingServices`, wraps the resulting iterator with `IOUserIterator::withIterator`, and releases the parsed object. The helper returns success after that construction without a separate null-output check; malformed dictionaries return `kIOReturnBadArgument`. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2804).
io_service_get_matching_services_ool: First consumes the incoming VM copy with `vm_map_copyout(kernel_map, ...)`. After successful consumption it initializes the object output to null, puts dictionary/matching errors in the separate `result` output, and preserves RPC success so MIG handles outputs correctly. The common helper validates the main port, builds a compatibility-adjusted matching dictionary and iterator; temporary kernel mapping storage is then deallocated. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2776).
io_service_get_matching_service_bin: The common helper validates the main-device port, parses an `OSDictionary`, and applies the current task's compatibility rules. `IOService::copyMatchingService` returns a retained first matching service; absence is reported as `kIOReturnNotFound`, unlike the iterator-producing form. The parsed object is released regardless of matching outcome. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2887).
io_service_get_matching_service_ool: Maps/consumes the incoming VM-copy payload into `kernel_map`, initializes the service result to null, and calls the same dictionary/compatibility/`copyMatchingService` helper as the binary form. Once VM-copy consumption succeeds, operation failure is reported in the separate `result` field while the RPC return remains successful. The temporary mapping is deallocated after matching. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2859).
io_service_match_property_table_bin: The common helper first requires an `IOService`, then unserializes a dictionary, adjusts task compatibility matching and calls `service->passiveMatch`. It releases the dictionary after use. A well-formed dictionary can produce `matches = false` with success; failure to obtain a dictionary is a bad argument. This checks the supplied service rather than returning a global matching iterator. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2722).
io_service_match_property_table_ool: Consumes the OOL matching-data VM copy into `kernel_map`; after that succeeds, it invokes the common dictionary/compatibility/`passiveMatch` path and stores its status in `result`. Temporary mapped bytes are deallocated. Keeping the outer return successful after consuming the copy distinguishes operation errors from transport cleanup ownership. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L2696).
io_service_add_notification_bin: Checks the reference-word count against the corresponding 32-bit or 64-bit limit, copies supplied words into a zero-padded reference array, and passes its width to the common helper. That helper requires the main-device port and a bounded matching dictionary, chooses a notification message type, constructs `IOServiceUserNotification`, and registers a matching notifier. Failure invalidates the retained notification port and releases the wrapper; success attaches the notifier to the exported object. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3023).
io_service_add_notification_bin_64: Checks the reference-word count against the corresponding 32-bit or 64-bit limit, copies supplied words into a zero-padded reference array, and passes its width to the common helper. That helper requires the main-device port and a bounded matching dictionary, chooses a notification message type, constructs `IOServiceUserNotification`, and registers a matching notifier. Failure invalidates the retained notification port and releases the wrapper; success attaches the notifier to the exported object. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3049).
io_service_add_notification_ool: Validates and zero-pads the width-specific async reference array, then enters the OOL helper. Successful `vm_map_copyout` consumes the input copy, so the helper keeps transport success and reports matching/registration errors through `result`, with the notification output initially null. It deallocates the mapped dictionary bytes after the common notifier-construction path, whose failure cleanup invalidates the port and releases the wrapper. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3107).
io_service_add_notification_ool_64: Validates and zero-pads the width-specific async reference array, then enters the OOL helper. Successful `vm_map_copyout` consumes the input copy, so the helper keeps transport success and reports matching/registration errors through `result`, with the notification output initially null. It deallocates the mapped dictionary bytes after the common notifier-construction path, whose failure cleanup invalidates the port and releases the wrapper. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3133).
io_service_add_interest_notification: Validates and zero-pads the appropriate async-reference width, requires an `IOService`, interns the interest name, and builds an `IOServiceMessageUserNotification` around the supplied port. `registerInterest` supplies the notifier retained by that wrapper; failure invalidates the port and releases it. The common body also contains WatchOS power-interest entitlement checking, with enforcement controlled by `gEnforcePowerEntitlement`. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3244).
io_service_add_interest_notification_64: Validates and zero-pads the appropriate async-reference width, requires an `IOService`, interns the interest name, and builds an `IOServiceMessageUserNotification` around the supplied port. `registerInterest` supplies the notifier retained by that wrapper; failure invalidates the port and releases it. The common body also contains WatchOS power-interest entitlement checking, with enforcement controlled by `gEnforcePowerEntitlement`. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3266).
io_service_acknowledge_notification: Requires an `IOService`, converts the numeric notification reference into `IONotificationRef` and passes the response bits to the service's virtual `acknowledgeNotification`. The wrapper returns that operation's result directly. It does not validate acknowledgement state itself or treat the reference as a Mach port name. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3289).
io_connect_get_notification_semaphore: Requires an `IOUserClient`, records client-call statistics and enters its write IPC gate. It delegates the requested notification type to `getNotificationSemaphore`, exits the gate and returns the driver's result. The output semaphore is a separate kernel object translated by MIG; the wrapper does not create a generic semaphore for every notification type. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3302).
io_registry_get_root_entry: Requires `main_device_port`, obtains the registry root and explicitly retains it if present before assigning the object output. The wrapper returns success even if the root pointer is null. The retained nonnull object is supplied to the outgoing object/capability translation rather than exposed as a raw kernel pointer. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3321).
io_registry_create_iterator: Requires the main-device port, resolves the named registry plane, and invokes `IORegistryIterator::iterateOver` with the requested options. The registry iterator is wrapped in `IOUserIterator` for export. A null result returns `kIOReturnBadArgument`; the wrapper does not itself walk the graph or return a snapshot array of all entries. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3342).
io_registry_entry_create_iterator: Requires an `IORegistryEntry` capability and constructs traversal from that entry in the named plane with the caller's options. `IOUserIterator::withIterator` supplies the exported wrapper; failure yields `kIOReturnBadArgument`. This anchors iteration at an already authorized object rather than requiring the global main-device port. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3361).
io_registry_iterator_enter_entry: The `CHECKLOCKED` path obtains an `IORegistryIterator` from the exported user iterator. The wrapper holds the enclosing iterator lock while calling `enterEntry`, then unlocks and returns success. This mutates traversal position; it does not attach the entry to a new registry plane. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3378).
io_registry_iterator_exit_entry: After validating the wrapped registry iterator, it holds the user iterator lock around `exitEntry`. A successful ascent returns success; inability to exit the current traversal level returns `kIOReturnNoDevice`. Lock release occurs before either result is returned. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3392).
io_registry_entry_from_path: Requires `main_device_port` and calls `IORegistryEntry::fromPath`. If that fails and task registry compatibility is active, it builds a dictionary containing compatibility and path-match keys and asks `copyMatchingService` for a fallback. Temporary dictionary/string objects are released. The output may remain null while the wrapper still returns success. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3408).
io_registry_entry_from_path_ool: Requires the main-device port and prefers the nonempty in-band path. Otherwise it requires a bounded nonempty OOL payload, consumes its VM copy and checks the final byte is null. It calls `fromPath`, reports not-found or malformed-path status in `result`, and deallocates mapped bytes. After consuming the VM copy, transport success is preserved even when lookup fails; this body lacks the legacy wrapper's compatibility fallback. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3443).
io_registry_entry_in_plane: Requires an `IORegistryEntry`, resolves the named plane and calls `inPlane` on that entry. The output Boolean reports membership with RPC success. The wrapper neither traverses parents nor rewrites graph relationships; interpretation of a missing plane is delegated to the registry operation. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3505).
io_registry_entry_get_path: Requires an `IORegistryEntry` and supplies the fixed `io_string_t` capacity to `getPath` for the named plane. Successful formatting returns success; failure returns `kIOReturnBadArgument`. No second larger buffer or partial-path recovery is attempted by this legacy fixed-size form. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3520).
io_registry_entry_get_path_ool: Attempts `getPath` in the small in-band buffer first, with OOL output initialized empty. If that fails, it allocates a 16-KiB temporary buffer and retries, returning no-memory or formatting error as appropriate. Success converts those bytes to outgoing VM-copy data through `copyoutkdata`; temporary allocation is freed in all fallback cases. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3538).
io_registry_entry_get_name: Requires an `IORegistryEntry` and copies `getName()` into the fixed `io_name_t` array using the body’s `strncpy`. It returns success without allocating or exporting another object. The result is a bounded name field; it is not a full path or an independently retained registry name object. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3579).
io_registry_entry_get_name_in_plane: Requires an `IORegistryEntry`; a nonempty plane name is resolved, while an empty name passes a null plane. It copies the selected `getName(plane)` into the fixed output with `strncpy`. This asks for the registry entry's name in that context without traversing or changing its plane membership. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3592).
io_registry_entry_get_location_in_plane: Requires an `IORegistryEntry`, resolves a nonempty plane name or uses null for an empty name, then reads `getLocation`. A present location is copied into the fixed output; absence yields `kIOReturnNotFound`. Location and entry name are distinct registry properties and this call does not synthesize a path from them. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3613).
io_registry_entry_get_registry_entry_id: Requires an `IORegistryEntry` and copies `getRegistryEntryID()` into the 64-bit result. This returns the registry's identity value for the current object, not a memory address, process ID, or Mach port name. It neither searches by ID nor extends lifetime beyond the ordinary object-call reference. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3639).
io_registry_entry_get_child_iterator: Requires an `IORegistryEntry`, resolves the requested plane, obtains the corresponding child or parent iterator, and wraps it with `IOUserIterator::withIterator` for export. The visible wrapper returns success without an explicit null-result test. Plane graph ownership and iterator invalidation remain in the registry/iterator implementations. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4220).
io_registry_entry_get_parent_iterator: Requires an `IORegistryEntry`, resolves the requested plane, obtains the corresponding child or parent iterator, and wraps it with `IOUserIterator::withIterator` for export. The visible wrapper returns success without an explicit null-result test. Plane graph ownership and iterator invalidation remain in the registry/iterator implementations. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4235).
io_registry_entry_get_property: Requires a registry entry and passes the configured MAC property-read check. `IOCopyPropertyCompatible` returns a retained ordinary property or allowed compatibility-overlay value. The wrapper serializes it into `OSSerialize`, converts the serialized bytes to outgoing VM-copy data with `copyoutkdata`, and releases both objects. Missing properties, allocation failure and unsupported serialization have distinct errors. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3758).
io_registry_entry_get_property_bytes: After entry/MAC validation, obtains a retained compatible property and exports only supported scalar/data forms: serializable `OSData`, string including null, Boolean as `Yes`/`No`, or the number's bounded byte width. Other object types return a bad argument. A too-small output buffer returns `kIOReturnIPCError`; the retained property is always released after conversion. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3684).
io_registry_entry_get_property_recursive: Requires the entry and MAC approval, then calls `copyProperty(name, plane, options)` to obtain a retained property through registry traversal. It serializes the found object into the outgoing VM-copy representation, releasing serializer and property afterward. Missing property is `kIOReturnNotFound`; this older wrapper has one initial MAC check rather than the per-candidate checks visible in the newer binary-buffer routine. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3803).
io_registry_entry_get_properties: This exact legacy body returns `kIOReturnUnsupported` immediately. It does not serialize the entry's dictionary. The binary variants below implement property-table export and filtering, so their behavior must not be attributed to this retained compatibility slot. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3851).
io_registry_entry_get_properties_bin: Delegates to the buffer-capable binary implementation with a null direct destination and no size pointer, forcing the outgoing VM-copy representation. The common implementation applies optional MAC filtering during serialization and merges allowed compatibility overlays into a temporary property dictionary. It releases serializer and temporary property objects after producing output; this wrapper adds no independent property snapshot. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3979).
io_registry_entry_get_properties_bin_buf: Builds a binary serializer, optionally installing a MAC editor that filters top-level properties. Compatibility overlays are merged into a temporary property dictionary with overlay-container keys removed; otherwise `serializeProperties` supplies the table. If the caller's direct buffer fits, copyout fills it and OOL output is empty. Otherwise it returns VM-copy data and clears the direct-buffer size. Serialization/copy errors are returned after releasing temporary objects. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3894).
io_registry_entry_get_property_bin: Calls the binary-buffer implementation with no direct output buffer, so successful serialization returns OOL VM-copy data. The common path handles property-key enumeration, compatibility lookup, optional recursive traversal and remove-on-read properties, with configured MAC checks. It releases the retained property after serialization; the wrapper does not bypass those checks merely because its result is OOL. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4091).
io_registry_entry_get_property_bin_buf: Checks the entry/property MAC rule, interns the key, then either obtains property keys or performs compatible lookup, including optional recursive traversal and per-candidate MAC checks. A found remove-on-read property is removed before serialization/output. It returns binary bytes through a sufficiently large direct user buffer or OOL copy, releasing symbol, iterator, serializer and property references. A later copy failure does not restore a removed property. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L3990).
io_registry_entry_set_properties: Bounds and consumes the OOL VM copy, unserializes it and deallocates mapped bytes. It checks MAC policy and any allowable-key array before dispatching `setProperties`, with user-client or property-action locking selected by the entry's settings. DriverKit services can then invoke `UserSetProperties`. Parsed objects and allowable-key references are released. Once the input copy is consumed, operation status goes in `result`, while the outer return reflects copy consumption. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4106).
io_service_get_busy_state: Requires an `IOService` and exports `getBusyState` as a scalar. This reads the service's busy accounting; it does not wait for matching/configuration to complete and does not itself acquire a termination claim. The wrapper returns success with whatever value the service method supplies. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4250).
io_service_get_state: Requires an `IOService` and reads `getState`, `getBusyState` and `getAccumulatedBusyTime` into separate outputs. The body performs three method calls without wrapping them in a common snapshot lock, so the outputs should not be described as an atomic multi-field state snapshot. No waiting or state transition is requested. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4263).
io_service_wait_quiet: Requires an `IOService`, converts the supplied seconds/nanoseconds pair to a 64-bit nanosecond timeout, then returns `service->waitQuiet(timeoutNS)`. Busy-state waiting and timeout handling occur in that service method. The wrapper does not drain a specific workloop or independently acknowledge power notifications. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4280).
io_service_wait_quiet_with_options: Requires an `IOService` and converts the timeout to nanoseconds. If the caller requests `kIOWaitQuietPanicOnFailure` without its entitlement, the wrapper logs and removes that option rather than rejecting the entire wait. It then calls `waitQuietWithOptions` with the resulting flags and returns the service's outcome. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4297).
io_service_request_probe: Requires an `IOService` and forwards the option bits to its virtual `requestProbe`, returning the result directly. This is a driver/service probe request, not a direct instruction to instantiate every matching personality. Supported options and effects depend on the selected service implementation. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4325).
io_service_get_authorization_id: Requires an `IOService` and first checks administrator privilege through `IOUserClient::clientHasPrivilege`. On macOS it exports the service's authorization ID; on other targets it writes zero and returns unsupported. The ID query therefore has its own explicit privilege check independent of the object-capability lookup. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4336).
io_service_set_authorization_id: Requires an `IOService`; on macOS it delegates to `setAuthorizationID`, while other targets return unsupported. Unlike the adjacent getter wrapper, this body contains no separate administrator-privilege check, so admission and any additional authorization must be understood from capability translation and the called service method rather than copied from the getter's contract. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4362).
io_service_open_extended: Requires an `IOService`, the current task as owner and MAC approval; nonnull properties are unsupported in the active body. `newUserClient` constructs the client, after which the wrapper initializes locking/shared-instance settings, enforces IOUserClient2022 property requirements and entitlement/MAC/filter policy, then registers ownership. Later failure calls `clientClose`, clears termination deferral and releases the client. Successful transport returns the client and a separate operation `result`; early validation errors return directly. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4377).
io_service_close: An `OSSet` mapping capability is accepted as a compatibility no-op. Otherwise the object must be an `IOUserClient`. A shared instance or successful atomic closed-bit transition enters the write IPC gate and calls `clientClose`; repeated nonshared closes are logged and ignored. The wrapper returns success rather than propagating `clientClose`'s result. Closing the logical connection is distinct from deallocating its Mach send-right name. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4613).
io_connect_get_service: Requires an `IOUserClient`, enters its IPC lifetime gate with no client lock request and obtains `getService`. It retains a nonnull service before leaving the gate and assigning the output capability. Missing backing service returns unsupported; an existing service returns success with a reference suitable for outgoing object translation. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4639).
io_connect_set_notification_port: Requires an `IOUserClient`, records call statistics, enters the write IPC gate and invokes the driver's `registerNotificationPort` with notification type, port and reference. The older form widens its 32-bit reference; the 64-bit form passes the user reference directly. Gate exit precedes return of the driver's result. This registers a callback destination rather than immediately sending a notification. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4663).
io_connect_set_notification_port_64: Requires an `IOUserClient`, records call statistics, enters the write IPC gate and invokes the driver's `registerNotificationPort` with notification type, port and reference. The older form widens its 32-bit reference; the 64-bit form passes the user reference directly. Gate exit precedes return of the driver's result. This registers a callback destination rather than immediately sending a notification. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4684).
io_connect_map_shared_memory: Requires a nonshared user client and the current task as target. Under the configured IPC gate, it gets `clientMemoryForType`, requires an `OSData` sharing context, checks writable-sharing entitlement and output-description capacity, then creates an anywhere mapping with permitted user options. Success exports address/size and stores the mapping in the client's set under `gIOObjectPortLock`, releasing the temporary mapping reference. Sharing-description copy and mapping creation are separate failure points. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4706).
io_connect_map_memory_into_task: Requires a user client and target task, then calls `mapClientMemory64` under the configured IPC gate. A mapping exports address/size. Shared instances or another target task attempt to create a mapping-object send right in that task. An ordinary current-task mapping is inserted into `client->mappings` when its set exists or can be allocated, under `gIOObjectPortLock`. The temporary map reference is released. The wrapper returns success when a map was obtained without separately checking port creation, set allocation or set insertion; absence of a map returns bad argument. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4797-L4855).
io_connect_map_memory: Widens the input 32-bit address and size using `SCALAR64`, delegates to `is_io_connect_map_memory_into_task`, and narrows the resulting values using `SCALAR32` before returning the delegated status. Thus mapping ownership, target-task admission and IPC gating are inherited from the wide implementation; this compatibility wrapper does not implement an independent physical-memory mapping path or explicit overflow-result branch. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4859).
io_connect_unmap_memory_from_task: Requires a client and task, obtains the descriptor for the memory type, and uses `kIOMapReference` to locate a mapping at the address. It removes that map from the client set under the object-port lock. Shared/other-task mappings attempt to create a temporary send right; only a nonzero returned name selects `userClientUnmap` and the two-send-reference decrement, whose result is overwritten by success. Otherwise it releases the exported object port. Temporary map-reference release depends on the shared/other-task branch. Missing referenced mapping returns bad argument. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4911-L4971).
io_connect_unmap_memory: This compatibility wrapper forwards the supplied 32-bit address, task and memory type to `is_io_connect_unmap_memory_from_task`. The wide routine performs descriptor lookup, reference-mapping lookup, client-set removal and exported-port cleanup. The local temporary widened address does not create another mapping or change the argument actually passed to the wide helper. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4975).
io_connect_add_client: Requires both capabilities to identify `IOUserClient` objects. The initiating client enters its configured write-or-none IPC gate, calls its virtual `connectClient` with the second client, exits the gate and returns the method's status. The wrapper does not itself merge the clients' mappings or owners; any connection-specific relationship is implemented by that virtual method. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L4994).
io_connect_set_properties: Directly delegates the connection capability and OOL property payload to `is_io_registry_entry_set_properties`. That shared path handles VM-copy consumption, object parsing, MAC/allowable-key policy, locking and `setProperties`/DriverKit forwarding. Consequently operation failure can be reported through the separate `result` after successful consumption rather than by failing the outer RPC. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L5015).
io_connect_method: Builds `IOExternalMethodArguments`, clears reserved/output-scalar storage and represents large user buffers with task memory descriptors: input uses copy-on-write plus `kIODirectionOut`, output uses `kIODirectionIn`. It rejects OOL lengths that belong in-band and oversized output lengths, applies the per-task external-method filter, then calls `callExternalMethod`. Updated output counts are copied back and temporary descriptors released. [Call gating](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L6583) selects client locking and legacy versus 2022 dispatch; driver selectors define the operation. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L5133).
io_connect_async_method: Requires at least one reference word, replaces word zero with the wake port and marks 64-bit userspace references when appropriate. It constructs the same scalar/structure/descriptor arguments as the synchronous form, but applies the async-method filter and supplies the async reference and port to `callExternalMethod`. Output counts and temporary descriptor cleanup are synchronous; a later completion notification is a separate driver operation, not automatic completion of the MIG request. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L5236).
io_connect_method_var_output: Builds synchronous external-method arguments with a pointer for driver-produced variable-output ownership, optionally representing large input with a copy-on-write descriptor. After filtering and dispatch, success requires the output object to be `OSSerialize` or `OSData`; data is clipped for copyout and converted into outgoing VM-copy bytes. Other output types yield underrun. Input descriptor and returned object are released, including after serialization/copy failure; scalar/in-band counts are propagated separately. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L5026).
io_connect_method_scalarI_scalarO: Widens the legacy scalar input array to 64-bit words and zeroes a temporary wide output array. It delegates to `is_io_connect_method` with no structure or OOL buffers, then narrows the returned scalar words using the updated output count, returning the shared method status. Selector validation, policy and IPC gating remain in the shared dispatch path rather than this ABI adapter. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L5350).
io_connect_method_scalarI_structureO: Widens legacy scalar inputs and calls the unified synchronous method path with the in-band structure output and its capacity/count pointer. Scalar output and OOL sizes are explicitly zero. The driver-updated structure size comes back through the original count pointer; policy and selector behavior are inherited from `is_io_connect_method` and the selected client's implementation. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L5733).
io_connect_method_scalarI_structureI: Widens legacy scalar input words, forwards the supplied in-band input structure, and initializes all output counts to zero before calling `is_io_connect_method`. This form has no scalar, structure or OOL output payload. It still uses the shared external-method filter, client gate and driver selector dispatch; a successful RPC need not imply any generic kernel-side state change beyond the driver's chosen operation. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L5906).
io_connect_method_structureI_structureO: Adapts the legacy in-band structure-input/structure-output form to `is_io_connect_method`, with scalar input absent and scalar/OOL output counts zero. The shared dispatcher receives the actual structure buffers and sizes and updates the output count. Any legacy target-method shape validation occurs below that common path, not in a new independent implementation of the selector. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L6083).
io_async_method_scalarI_scalarO: Checks the legacy async-reference count, widens supplied reference words and zero-pads unused slots. It widens scalar inputs, zeroes a wide output array and calls the unified async method with no structure/OOL buffers. Returned scalar words are narrowed using the updated count. The common async path rewrites reference word zero with the wake port and performs policy/dispatch; later notification lifetime remains a separate concern. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L5464).
io_async_method_scalarI_structureO: Bounds and widens/zero-pads the legacy async references, widens scalar inputs and delegates to `is_io_connect_async_method` with an in-band structure output. Scalar output and OOL counts start at zero. The shared path records the wake port, applies async policy and invokes the client's method, while the caller's structure output count carries the synchronous reply size. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L5515).
io_async_method_scalarI_structureI: Bounds, widens and zero-pads the async-reference array, widens scalar inputs and forwards the in-band input structure. It initializes all output counts to zero and calls the shared async method. This wrapper packages a legacy input-only method call; it does not itself send an asynchronous completion or retain an arbitrary userspace buffer after return. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L5558).
io_async_method_structureI_structureO: Validates and widens/zero-pads the legacy async references, then supplies in-band structure input/output to the unified async method with no scalar buffers and no OOL output. The output count is passed through to receive the driver's synchronous structure length. Wake-port encoding, filtering, client gating and any later asynchronous notification use the shared implementation. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L5602).
io_catalog_send_data: Under production `NO_KEXTD`, returns not-privileged. Otherwise it requires the main port and command-appropriate data; missing management entitlement intentionally returns outer success without applying changes. Input VM-copy data is bounded, consumed, parsed and unmapped. The command switch calls catalogue reset/add/remove-driver operations, optionally starting matching; removed/kextd-state commands return unsupported. After copy consumption, operation status is returned through `result` and the parsed object is released. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L6205).
io_catalog_terminate: Requires the main-device port and administrator privilege. Outside `SECURE_KERNEL`, the flag selects `terminateDrivers` for a named service or `terminateDriversForModule`, with module-unload determining whether unloading is requested. Unsupported flags, including the excluded commands in secure builds, return bad argument. Termination coordination is delegated to the catalogue rather than completed by merely decoding the request. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L6340).
io_catalog_get_data: Requires the main-device port, creates a serializer and invokes `gIOCatalogue->serializeData(flag, ...)`. On success it allocates tagged kernel VM, copies serialized bytes there and uses `vm_map_copyin` with source destruction to construct the outgoing OOL result. Serializer allocation, catalogue selection, VM allocation and VM-copy conversion can fail separately; the serializer is released before return. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L6380).
io_catalog_get_gen_count: Requires the main-device port and a nonnull output pointer, then reads `gIOCatalogue->getGenerationCount` into the result. This reports catalogue generation rather than returning matching services or a versioned property snapshot. The wrapper does not hold a collection iterator or trigger driver matching as a side effect. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L6425).
io_catalog_module_loaded: Requires the main-device port and a nonnull module name, calls `gIOCatalogue->moduleHasLoaded(name)` and returns success. The wrapper is a notification to catalogue matching machinery; it does not load module bytes, validate a code signature, or prove a requested module actually became executable. Those actions belong to other paths. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L6448).
io_catalog_reset: Requires the main-device port and recognizes only `kIOCatalogResetDefault`. That selector calls `gIOCatalogue->reset` and the wrapper returns success; all other flags yield bad argument. Unlike adjacent catalogue operations, this visible wrapper contains no separate administrator or management-entitlement check, so its actual admission must be read with the capability boundary rather than inferred from neighboring handlers. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L6468).
io_device_tree_entry_exists_with_name: Requires the main-device port and interprets an optional colon as an entry-name/property-name separator. It recursively searches device-tree entries with `IODTFindMatchingEntries`, examines only the first matching entry, and returns true when that entry exists and the requested property, if any, exists. The iterator is released; absence is a false Boolean with successful RPC, not a lookup error. [Local implementation](../../../platydoc-data/xnu/iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp#L6547).
